about.title: Chino Hills Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You catch yourself on a wet grocery aisle, a cracked walkway outside a Peyton Drive storefront, or an unlit stairwell at an apartment complex, and your first thought is embarrassment, not evidence. Yet in California, whether a property owner is responsible turns on a specific question: did they know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That element, called notice, is where most Chino Hills premises cases are won or lost. Surveillance footage from a shopping center along Chino Hills Parkway can show how long a spill sat unattended. A photo taken before a manager mops the floor can preserve what the scene really looked like. We handle premises liability claims on contingency, so you owe no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Chino Hills Residents Choose Us

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires proof the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Our team focuses early on incident reports, inspection logs and store video before that evidence disappears.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than You'd Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but a fall on city, county or state property in Chino Hills triggers a much shorter claim window. Getting started quickly protects your options.

items.title: Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, being distracted or wearing the wrong shoes may reduce a recovery but does not erase it. We can push back when an insurer tries to pin everything on you.

items.question: I fell on a sidewalk or at a park owned by the City of Chino Hills. Is that different from falling in a store?
items.answer: Yes, and the difference matters a lot. Claims against a public entity in California must usually be presented as a government claim within six months, far sooner than the two-year deadline that applies to private owners. Photograph the exact spot, note the nearest cross street, and contact us promptly so we can evaluate whether a government claim needs to be filed.

items.question: The store already cleaned up the spill before I could take pictures. Do I still have a case?
items.answer: Possibly. Most retail locations along Chino Hills Parkway and Peyton Drive run surveillance cameras, and that footage can show both the hazard and how long it sat there. We can send a preservation letter right away, because many systems overwrite video within days or weeks. Your own account, any witnesses, and the incident report you request from the manager also help fill in the picture.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact you about a fall?
items.answer: No. There is no charge to contact us or for us to review your case. We handle premises liability claims on contingency, meaning you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
